sources.title: Analyse du paysage climatique pour les enfants aux Comores
geographic_coverage: coastal and riverine areas across the islands
sources.temporal_coverage: Observed island-level water access; modeled rainfall and sea-level risks to 2090; May 2024 flood impacts.
sources.methodology: UNICEF climate-landscape assessment using secondary evidence and youth consultations.
sources.limitations: National assessment with limited local exposure and displacement estimates.

sources.title: Comoros National Water Resilience Project (P504691) – Additional Financing Request 1
sources.temporal_coverage: Project appraisal context and water-sector conditions documented in April 2025.
sources.methodology: Public-disclosure appraisal-stage project information document with country and water-sector context.
sources.limitations: Project document summarizing sector estimates; it is not an independent national water-sector evaluation.

sources.title: Inondation en mai- juin 2024 : Une main forte extraordinaire dans les zones sinistrées
sources.temporal_coverage: May 2024 floods and response measures reported through September 2024.
sources.methodology: UNDP article reporting official flood response, affected localities and follow-up works.
sources.limitations: News report, not a comprehensive damage assessment or independent response evaluation.

sources.title: Increased Access to Water Supply for Resilience in Comoros (IAWASuR)
sources.temporal_coverage: Project status milestones through August 2025 and planned cross-island water-resilience activities.
sources.methodology: Official project summary, intended beneficiaries, expected outcomes and approval milestones.
sources.limitations: The page describes aims and expected outcomes, not verified implementation results.

claims.locator: Printed pp. 30–31 (PDF pp. 37–38), section 3.2.4, water access by island
claims.paraphrase: UNICEF reports about half Grande Comore's upland population relies on rainwater; Anjouan and Mohéli households mainly use gravity-fed rivers that often dry seasonally.
claims.limitations: Island-level profiles do not provide named-village estimates.

claims.locator: Printed p. 31 (PDF p. 38), section 3.2.4, future rainfall and water scarcity
claims.paraphrase: The assessment projects dry-season rainfall to fall 47% by 2090 and says more irregular precipitation may prolong drought and worsen freshwater scarcity.
claims.scenario: The cited UNICEF passage does not specify an emissions scenario.

claims.locator: PDF pp. 14–15, climate-risk table, sea-level-rise and cyclone/flood/landslide rows
claims.paraphrase: UNICEF projects 20 cm of sea-level rise by 2050 and displacement of about 10% of coastal residents; its hazard table also lists family separation and possible child exposure to violence.
claims.scenario: The table presents these as potential impacts but does not specify a climate emissions scenario.
claims.limitations: National risk assessment; cited passages do not map local displacement sites or attribute violence to conflict.
claims.source_stated_fcv_link: UNICEF links hazards to potential displacement and family separation, and says separation may elevate children's exposure to violence; it does not identify conflict.

claims.locator: Article paragraphs on May 2024 flooding and affected localities; web-page paragraphs 34–39, no page numbering
claims.paraphrase: May 2024 heavy rains flooded Fomboni and Wanani (Mohéli), Vouani and Moya (Anjouan), and Bangoi and Moroni (Grande Comore); UNDP reports 66,835 people affected across the islands and three deaths.
claims.limitations: Affected totals are island-wide; locality-specific loss totals are not provided.

claims.locator: Article paragraphs on contingency-plan activation and multisector assessments; paragraphs 36–38
claims.paraphrase: The Civil Protection directorate activated the national contingency plan and a fixed command post; nine multisector teams from national actors, Red Cross, MSF and UN agencies conducted initial assessments.
claims.limitations: The article reports mobilization and initial assessments, not an independent response evaluation.

claims.locator: Article paragraphs on funded river/drain works and return to homes; paragraphs 41–53
claims.paraphrase: UNDP reports KMF 77 million funded 45-day river/drain clearance and rock removal in named communities; it later reports families in Mitsoudje returned home after channel clearing.
claims.limitations: The article reports activities and near-term return, not evidence of reduced future risk.
claims.source_stated_fcv_link: The article says floods displaced families and reports their return to homes after channel clearing; it does not discuss conflict.

claims.locator: PDF p. 5 (printed p. 3), country context, paragraph 4
claims.paraphrase: The Bank says climate impacts add to population and resource pressures in Grand Moroni, which receives most national rural-to-urban migration; internal migration accounts for an estimated 78% of city population growth.
claims.limitations: The PID summarizes existing studies; it does not estimate climate-attributable migration.

claims.locator: PDF p. 6 (printed p. 4), sectoral context, paragraph 5
claims.paraphrase: In Grand Moroni, basic household access masks unaffordable, unreliable or unsafe water; rainwater supplies 35.8% of Comorians, piped service runs about two hours daily, and tanker water costs 4–10 times official tariffs.
institutions: Ministry of Energy, Water and Hydrocarbons
claims.limitations: PID figures are sector estimates; affordability and reliability vary within Grand Moroni.

claims.locator: PDF p. 6 (printed p. 4), sectoral context, paragraph 7
claims.paraphrase: The Bank says years of political instability damaged the water sector, leaving aged infrastructure and persistent gaps in water management, investment, oversight, cost recovery and maintenance.
affected_groups: households reliant on public water services
claims.limitations: The PID does not identify conflict episodes or quantify political-instability effects on climate adaptation.
claims.source_stated_fcv_link: The Bank explicitly says years of political instability were detrimental to water-sector management and infrastructure development.

claims.locator: Project summary, beneficiaries, expected outcomes and approval milestones
claims.paraphrase: IAWASuR aims to benefit 75,000 people (51% women) across Anjouan, Mohéli and Grande Comore through watershed restoration, climate-resilient water infrastructure, climate-smart governance and institutional capacity-building.
claims.limitations: Beneficiary figures and expected outputs are project aims, not verified achieved coverage or outcomes.

search_audit.query: Comoros climate vulnerability water drought floods local island differences Anjouan Mohéli Grande Comore report
search_audit.outcome: Read UNICEF's full country landscape, the World Bank Grand Moroni water PID and UNDP's flood article; identified island-specific water dependence and named 2024 flood localities. No village-level water-access estimates were found.

search_audit.query: Comoros climate change water stress displacement child violence conflict resource competition report
search_audit.outcome: UNICEF identifies hazard-related displacement and family separation, with potential increased child exposure to violence, but does not attribute violence to conflict. No inspected new source explicitly links climate stress to armed conflict or violent disputes.

search_audit.query: Comoros political instability conflict effects water sector climate adaptation infrastructure report
search_audit.outcome: The World Bank PID says years of political instability were detrimental to water-sector management and infrastructure development; it does not name specific conflict episodes or quantify effects on climate adaptation.

search_audit.query: Comoros local flood response early warning recovery climate resilient water capacity UNDP 2024 2025
search_audit.outcome: UNDP reports contingency-plan activation, multiagency assessments and funded river/drain works; its adaptation page gives planned cross-island water, watershed and institutional-capacity targets, not evaluated outcomes.

gaps: No inspected source explicitly states that climate stress caused armed conflict or violent disputes in Comoros. UNICEF identifies potential hazard-related displacement and family separation with possible child exposure to violence; the World Bank separately reports political instability's harm to the water sector without linking it to climate impacts.
Public evidence reviewed gives island-level water vulnerability and named flood localities, but little water-access or displacement detail below island/Grand Moroni scale.
UNICEF projections are national and scenario-unspecified; the UNDP IAWASuR page reports intended targets and expected outcomes rather than verified results.
A UNICEF community-resilience article page timed out on direct access and was not used.
